**Count matrices by their dimensions, then multiply repeated blocks.** Standard multi-head attention with model width d has query, key, value, and output projections, each roughly d by d: four d squared parameters. A two-matrix feed-forward block contributes $2dd_{ff}$. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762)

With feed-forward width 4d, one block contributes 12d squared before smaller terms. L blocks plus one tied vocabulary embedding table give $12Ld^2+Vd$ under these assumptions.

**A numerical example.** With d=512, L=12, and V=32,000, blocks contribute about 37.75 million parameters and tied embeddings about 16.38 million, for roughly 54.13 million before biases and norms. Untying the output table adds another 16.38 million.

Gated FFNs have three matrices, GQA changes key/value projection sizes, and MoE adds expert parameters that may not all activate per token. Learned positional tables, biases, and final normalization also matter. State the architecture before calling a formula exact. Parameter count, active computation, and activation memory are related but distinct quantities.

**Technical details and references.**

Ignoring biases, normalization parameters, and positional embeddings, standard MHA has four $d\times d$ projections per layer, contributing $4d^2$. A two-matrix FFN contributes $2dd_{ff}$. With tied token embeddings the total is $L(4d^2+2dd_{ff})+Vd$. Setting $d_{ff}=4d$ gives $12Ld^2+Vd$. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762)

That expression is not an exact universal Transformer count. With projection biases and two affine LayerNorms, a common block adds $9d+d_{ff}$ parameters; a final LayerNorm adds $2d$. Learned positional embeddings, untied output weights, output biases, gated FFNs, GQA, and MoE alter the result. Specify the actual architecture and whether embeddings/norms are shared. For a gated FFN with three matrices, substitute $3dd_{ff}$ for the two-matrix FFN term.
